bib.title: CodeXGLUE: A Machine Learning Benchmark Dataset for Code Understanding and Generation
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2021 Datasets and Benchmarks Track (venue not printed in the PDF text; preprint arXiv:2102.04664v2)

read.skipped: References (from about char 51848) skimmed only for lineage.

question: Can a single GLUE-style benchmark of diverse code understanding and generation tasks, with baseline systems and an evaluation platform, speed up research on code intelligence?
hypothesis: A diversified benchmark, as ImageNet and GLUE were for vision and NLP, will accelerate applied AI research on code (implied by the introduction).
contributions: A benchmark of 10 tasks across 14 datasets (8 existing, the rest newly created) covering code-code, text-code, code-text and text-text
A platform for model evaluation and comparison
Three baseline systems: CodeBERT (BERT-style), CodeGPT (GPT-style, newly released) and an Encoder-Decoder framework

method.summary: Collects or builds 14 datasets for 10 code tasks, defines metrics and an overall score per task, and trains CodeBERT, CodeGPT and CodeBERT-initialised encoder-decoder baselines on each. Reports one results table per task plus training and inference time on 2 P100 GPUs.
method.task: code intelligence benchmark: clone detection, defect detection, cloze test, code completion, code repair, code translation, NL code search, text-to-code generation, code summarization, documentation translation

datasets.name: BigCloneBench
datasets.split: train/dev/test as given by Wang et al.
datasets.source: Svajlenko BigCloneBench [71], filtered by Wang et al. [84]
datasets.preprocessing: discard fragments without tagged true or false clone pairs

datasets.name: CT-all / CT-maxmin
datasets.split: test only, built from CodeSearchNet validation and test sets
datasets.source: CodeSearchNet [35]; CT-maxmin from CodeBERT PL-Probing data
datasets.preprocessing: 930 target tokens kept as unique words after BPE, punctuation removed by handcrafted rules, token occurrence thresholds set manually

datasets.name: PY150
datasets.size: 150,000 files; 100,000 train / 50,000 test; 76.3M and 37.2M tokens; dev 5K
datasets.preprocessing: tokenise, strip comments, strings over 15 characters replaced by empty string, <EOL> token added; line-level test set of 10,000 random lines with at least 15% of file as context; mean 489.11 input and 6.56 output tokens

datasets.name: Github Java Corpus
datasets.split: 1% subset following Hellendoorn and Devanbu and Karampatsis et al.
datasets.preprocessing: same as PY150 without <EOL>; line-level test 3,000 examples, mean 350.62 input and 10.49 output tokens

datasets.name: Bugs2Fix
datasets.source: Tufano et al. [75], GitHub Archive Mar 2011 to Oct 2017
datasets.preprocessing: names normalised, pairs with errors or over 100 AST edit actions dropped

datasets.name: CodeTrans (Java-C#)
datasets.source: Lucene, POI, JGit, Antlr (Itext and JTS excluded for licence)
datasets.preprocessing: match same signatures in similarly named classes, dedupe, drop pairs with token overlap under 1/3, null bodies, no data-flow; avg length 38.51 Java and 46.16 C# tokens

datasets.name: CodeSearchNet AdvTest
datasets.preprocessing: drop unparsable code, docs under 3 or over 256 tokens, docs with URLs, empty or non-English docs; function and variable names normalised to func and arg_i in dev/test; whole test set is the candidate pool

datasets.name: WebQueryTest
datasets.size: 1,300 labelled; 254 (-1), 642 (0), 422 (1); only classes 0 and 1 kept (642+422, derived)
datasets.source: real queries from a commercial search engine log containing python, candidates from CodeSearchNet
datasets.preprocessing: top 2 functions per query by a CodeBERT retrieval model trained on 148K StaQC; 13 developers annotated 100 each

datasets.name: CONCODE
datasets.size: 100,000 train, 4,000 dev and test (2K/2K in Table 1)

datasets.name: CodeSearchNet (summarization)
datasets.preprocessing: same four filter rules as AdvTest

datasets.name: Microsoft Docs
datasets.size: 43K, 19K, 44K, 50K training pairs for EN-LA, EN-DA, EN-NO, EN-ZH; 1K dev and 1K test each
datasets.preprocessing: drop identical pairs, under 3 words, length ratio over 3, fast_align alignment ratio under 0.6

models.architecture: 12-layer bidirectional Transformer encoder, MLM and replaced-token-detection pretraining

models.name: CodeGPT
models.architecture: GPT-2 architecture and objective, 12 decoder layers

models.name: CodeGPT-adapted
models.init_from: GPT-2, continued training on code corpus

other.note: default for completion and text-to-code; GPT-2 vocab size not stated separately

models.name: Encoder-Decoder
models.architecture: CodeBERT encoder + randomly initialised 6-layer Transformer decoder

other.documentation_translation: encoder from XLM-R, multilingual model with target-language token such as <2en>

models.name: RoBERTa, LSTM, BiLSTM, TextCNN, Transformer, GPT-2, Seq2Seq, PBSMT and prior task models

training.objective: CodeBERT MLM+RTD, CodeGPT next-token as GPT-2, fine-tuned per task with task losses (not detailed)
training.seq_len: max input 256 and max inference length 128 (code summarization only)
training.regularisation: early stopping on dev set (code summarization)
training.wall_clock: per task, Fig 8: e.g. 25 h PY150 completion, 30 h CONCODE, 30 h doc translation, 24 h code repair, 20 h translation, 12 h per language summarization

other.note: hyperparameters for all other tasks and for pretraining are not given in the paper

inference.retrieval: code search encodes text and code separately; AdvTest candidate pool is the whole test set, not 1,000

other.inference_time: Fig 8, e.g. 2 h BigCloneBench, 30 min PY150 on 2x P100

metrics.name: F1 / MAP (clone detection)
metrics.definition: F1 on BigCloneBench binary classification; MAP retrieving 499 programs on POJ-104; overall = mean

metrics.name: Token accuracy / exact match / Levenshtein edit similarity (completion)
metrics.definition: dataset score = mean of token accuracy and line edit similarity; overall = mean over both datasets

metrics.name: MRR; F1 and accuracy (code search)
metrics.definition: MRR on AdvTest; F1 and accuracy on WebQueryTest; overall = average of the values

metrics.name: EM accuracy, BLEU, CodeBLEU (code repair)
metrics.definition: exact match is the overall metric

metrics.name: smoothed BLEU (summarization, doc translation)
metrics.definition: summarization smoothed BLEU, overall mean over languages; doc translation BLEU averaged over 8 directions

baselines: prior clone detectors (RtvNN, Deckard, CDLH, ASTNN, FA-AST-GMN, TBCCD, code2vec, NCC, Aroma, MISIM-GNN)
eval.protocol: Single reported number per cell; no seeds, variance or significance tests stated. Leaderboard submissions by email.

limits: Only baselines are given, usually one run per cell; no variance, seeds or significance tests and most fine-tuning hyperparameters are unstated.
Models are small (about 125M) encoders and a GPT-2-small decoder; written in the BERT/GPT-2 era, so numbers are far below later code LLMs.
Metrics are overlap-based (BLEU, CodeBLEU, edit similarity, exact match) not execution-based; text-to-code has no functional tests.
Authors note the datasets are limited to six-ish languages and omit tasks such as idiom mining, bug localization, test generation and program synthesis, planned for future extension.
Authors say CodeBERT ignores code structure (AST, data flow) and improvement is limited on defect detection.
Code repair and defect detection results are low in absolute terms (62% accuracy, about 10% exact match).
Devign has no official split so authors made a random one; ambiguity over duplicate leakage not discussed.
